reference: limma::duplicateCorrelation(expr, design, block = block), then limma::lmFit(expr, design, block = block, correlation = consensus), then limma::eBayes(fit) and limma::eBayes(fit, trend = TRUE)
note: `expr` is features x samples (PRISM's orientation), `design` is samples x coef, `block` names each sample's subject. Matrices of results are features x coef. `atanh_correlations` are limma's per-feature values after its bounds are applied (nan where limma estimates none); `consensus_correlation` is tanh of their 15%-trimmed mean. `atanh_correlations_converged` re-solves each feature's REML fit to tol 1e-14 / maxit 1000 instead of limma's 1e-6 / 20, so the gap between the two is how tightly an independent REML optimizer can be held to limma. `global` is eBayes with a constant prior, `trend` with limma-trend's prior on Amean.

cases.name: nested_unequal_visits
cases.note: 7 subjects (28 samples) vs 8 subjects (35), 3-6 visits each, every subject in one group only; true intra-subject correlation 0.5 in every feature, a 1.0 log2 shift in the first 6. The case a fixed subject block cannot fit.

cases.name: singletons_and_covariate
cases.note: Four subjects contribute one sample (a block of size 1), and a subject-level numeric covariate, mean-centered as PRISM centers one, sits beside the group column.

cases.name: missing_values
cases.note: Scattered NA cells, so lmFit takes its per-feature GLS loop (the correlation matrix subset to each feature's observed samples) instead of one shared transform. F005 lacks every sample of subject A02; F009 keeps 4 values, too few for duplicateCorrelation, so its correlation is NA and excluded from the trimmed mean while its GLS fit still runs.

cases.name: time_by_group
cases.note: time + group + time:group with subject as the block - the combined within- and between-subject question. Every coefficient is pinned; the interaction (column 4) is the one a slope-difference test reads. A slope difference is planted in the first 5.

cases.name: correlation_bounds
cases.note: No subject effect in F001-F036, so some REML estimates fall below limma's floor 1/(1 - 8) + 0.01 and are raised to it; an overwhelming one in F037-F040 (sd 6 against residual 0.02), so those exceed 0.99 and are lowered to it. Null group effect.

degenerate.name: all_blocks_size_one
degenerate.note: every sample its own subject; limma warns and sets the correlation to 0

degenerate.name: block_in_design
degenerate.note: subject dummies already in the design (the paired design); limma warns and sets the correlation to 0
